source.title: Edge Flow: A Tractable and Predictive Continuous-Time Model for Gradient Descent at the Edge of Stability

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and figure captions.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates full-batch gradient descent dynamics at the edge of stability and compares its own model against those dynamics; this is a conceptual test of V5’s sharpness and loss behavior, not a direct replication of the cited studies.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own full-batch GD measurements of sharpness and training loss. The paper’s comparisons to Central Flow and its proposed Edge Flow method are not cataloged as separate results unless they report what GD itself does.
record.test_reason: The study measures full-batch GD training loss and Hessian sharpness, the same method and measures used for V5's edge-of-stability component. Its own GD trajectories bear on V5 independently of the proposed flow's performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors present Edge Flow as a tractable model that tracks tested full-batch GD trajectories and onset oscillations. Finer discretization and larger oscillation floors mitigate instabilities in EGD; analogous interventions in ordinary large-scale training remain suggestions rather than demonstrated results.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a continuous-time model and Edge Gradient Descent discretization, then compares them with full-batch GD; this is not a replication of the learning-rate studies named in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported onset behavior and stability depend on learning rate, discretization K, and the oscillation floor ε. The authors report GD divergence at η = 0.4 in the MLP setting.

fits_no_version.finding: EGD with K = 4 remains stable at η = 0.4 where GD diverges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refining the numerical integration of Edge Flow can extend EGD's stable learning-rate range.

record.problems: The experiments use small subsets of CIFAR-10 and one random seed. Most plotted GD values are not numerically tabulated. The paper notes that its derivation neglects higher-order coupled corrections and does not claim universal applicability.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for Edge Flow’s own loss and sharpness predictions, Central Flow comparisons, or the Rod Flow comparison: these are proposed/comparator methods rather than additional GD outcomes relevant to V5. Figure-only curves were retained where the text provides a qualitative result.

untested.parts: Training classification error, random-label memorization, and model-size, regularization or early-stopping comparisons.
ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effects of extra student neurons.
Controlled depth comparisons and effects of shortcuts or special initialization on training degradation.
Initialization comparisons, signal propagation, learning speed and maximum trainable depth.

The initial linearized-model threshold and catapult recovery in wide squared-loss networks; divergence demonstrated to begin below the stability threshold. Evidence covers finite training horizons on small CIFAR-10 subsets with one seed.
Batch normalization versus matched unnormalized networks, learning-rate tolerance attributable to normalization, and Fixup.

missing.what: Later exits from EoS in all three cross-entropy configurations; add distinct phase results rather than recording only onset.
GD sharpness settles somewhat above 2/η after several eigenvalues reach the edge, qualifying exact threshold equality.
GD reference outcomes at η = 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2 in the MLP learning-rate sweep, needed alongside the isolated η = 0.4 divergence result. Extract the GD curves separately from EGD.

record.verdict_notes: High-rate GD divergence is consistent with V5, so it does not itself warrant limits_scope. EGD's dependence on K or ε does not establish corresponding dependencies of ordinary GD. The modest above-threshold residual is compatible with hovering near the threshold.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 memorization, random or corrupted labels, and effects of model size or early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects on training error and the effects of identity shortcuts, special initialization, or normalization.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, or trainable depth.

The paper tests full-batch GD edge-of-stability behavior on small CIFAR-10 subsets, but not wide-network squared-loss experiments against the initial linearized model’s stability limit as specified in Lewkowycz et al.; it does not test the long-time sharpness behavior described by Cohen et al. across their original settings.
Batch normalization’s effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, or Fixup training without normalization.
